historical_references.reference: In medieval Europe, the name Eartha was a variant of the Old English name Eardwulf, which means 'earth wolf'. Eardwulf was the name of several Anglo-Saxon kings, including Eardwulf of Northumbria (r. 878-895 AD) and Eardwulf of Mercia (r. 874-879 AD), who were known for their military prowess and dominance over their respective territories.

During the Middle Ages, the name Eartha was also used as a feminine form of the Old English name Eorðan, which means 'giver of earth'. In this context, Eartha may have been considered a name for a woman who was nurturing and grounded, providing a connection to the earth and the natural world.
